main_text.l: Sanguine qui gaudet, sanguinolétus obit, Ut lupus agnellum sequitur, Cainus Abelu, Ut Iacobum Esau, legitimosq; nothi Sanguine tu fundata, pio nunc sanguine cre[?] Ergo cōcludam, Roma cruenta rues (fcis: Roma rues, quoniam uictrici turgida lauro, Antiquis spolijs foeta foeraxq; tuis: Inq; deauratis circumgestata quadrigis, Et satrapis mundi principibusq; præxes. Calcandus faftus, frangeda superbia: cedrus Alta ruit, sic tu Roma superba rues. Roma rues, mercesq; tuæ, thesaurus & ingës: Gemmas & coccum, thuraq; nullus emet, Et peris & perdes, occidis & occidis ipsa, Idq; malo merito uipera sæuo tuo. Roma rues, regnumq; tuū: uanescet & aurū, Nomē, apex, sceptrū, fulmia, mitra, thronꝰ Et cur Roma rues? prudēsq; uidēsq; peribis? Ergo uolens tibimet tu paris exitium? Dū fallis, falsa es: tua iam spelunca retecta est, Occulti coitus, frausq; Venusq; patent. Ergo tuas labes, & fœdas aspice sordes: Vitaq; nota alijs, sit quoq; nota tibi. Plurima Lutherus patefecit, Platina multa, Quædam Vergerius, cuncta Baleus habet. Ille tuam mouit Camerinam, motaq; foetet, Pandoræ Latiæ pyxis aperta uolat. Ille tuos cæcos uidit, prodituq; recessus: Furtiuos memorat, Roma petulca, thoros. Aulam lustrauit, rimas perspexit & omnes, Ingreditur

page.notes: The last word of line 4 is cut off by the fold: "cre[?]". The poem is printed in italic-free roman type with no marginal notes. The printed "Vtlupus" and "Vt Iacobum" are normalised to "Ut" per the u/v rule. Printed "tuū:uanescet" is read as "tuū: uanescet". Several words are doubtful at the scan's resolution, and only the first is marked [?].
